note: Day-2 register (Graph Engineering §VI.B). The paper's Day 2 is not 'have tools' — this harness has many — it is 'add ONE tool that addresses a MEASURED failure', with typed schema, permissions, and result confirmation, and the rung's exit criterion is that the tool REDUCES a known error class. This file supplies the link that was missing: for each tool, the error class it exists for, the artifact where that failure was written down, and the before/after rates. `reduces` stays null until BOTH rates are measured. That was true of every class when this note was written; it is now true of six of eight, FC-02 and FC-04 carrying `structural` reductions. The original finding stands for the rest and is not an omission: baselines exist where a failure was painful enough to measure, current rates almost nowhere — this harness measures its failures and not its fixes. The rung requires at least one sampled reduction; structural claims remain valid and stay labelled. A claim is only as good as the predicate its rate counted — FC-01's withdrawn v1.6.3 rate is the case study — and both that predicate and the model it was counted on must be recorded, or the number cannot be trusted the moment either one changes. WHY NO SAMPLED REDUCTION EXISTS, PER CLASS (2026-08-11, after day-2 rev 5). This is a derived result, not a backlog: with this register as it stands, the sampled reduction the rung asks for is not obtainable, and the reason differs by class. FC-01 — the class does not occur on the model under test: 0 of 8 scored Sonnet shapeup-sdlc rows ship nothing against 7 of 16 on Haiku, so there is no failure left to reduce; it is Haiku-scoped with reduces null, and the benchmark's MUT is now opus, on which it is rarer still. FC-05 — its registered tool IS the trigger-eval harness, an instrument that makes the class visible rather than a mechanism that reduces it; a measuring device cannot appear as the cause of its own reading. Its first measured rate (1d1da62) already showed fpr 0 across all 75 cross-skill negatives, so there is no before-state to reduce from, and manufacturing one from older descriptions would attribute incidental drift to a tool that did not act. FC-03, FC-06, FC-07, FC-08 — unmeasured on BOTH sides, and each registered tool is a hook, oracle or ledger that forbids its class by construction, so measuring them yields further STRUCTURAL claims, not sampled ones. WHAT WOULD REACH IT: a class not yet in this register, meeting three conditions at once — the failure occurs on the model under test, the tool is a mechanism rather than an instrument, and both rates are measurable on one model scope. That is new work with its own bet, not a remainder of day 2. The general shape is worth stating because it will recur: the stronger the model under test, the fewer of these failures occur at all, so a sampled reduction gets harder to buy exactly as the harness gets more capable — FC-01 is the worked example, 7/16 on Haiku to 0/8 on Sonnet.

classes.error_class: Narrated run — the orchestrator describes its own pipeline in future tense and stops, shipping nothing while reading like a clean run
classes.description: A tech-lead reached as args:"--unattended" lost the requirement text on the hand-off, printed eleven gate names and a plan, wrote no code, and scored 29% against a hidden acceptance suite with 10 escaped defects. Both pre-existing guards structurally could not see it.

discovered_by.quote: measured on sdd-harness-bench (F2 / Haiku 4.5, n=5, zero variance) … printed eleven gate names and a plan, wrote no code, and scored 29% while reading as a successful run

tool.name: gate-intake + run receipt
tool.permissions: PreToolUse deny on `Skill → tech-lead` with no resolvable intake; fails open on `--order` and on ambiguous arg shapes. Paired with skills/tech-lead/scripts/init-run.mjs, which must write .shapeup/<slug>/receipt.json as the run's first tool call.

result_confirmation.ref: structural §35 (init-run leaves the receipt), §37 (gate-zerowork blocks the narrated run and nothing else), §39 (valued flags stripped by the intake gate)

baseline.method: sdd-harness-bench F2, tech-lead dispatched as args:"--unattended" at harness_build a280e86 (git describe: v1.3.0-15-ga280e86); the pathology occurred in all five runs (zero variance) — FINDINGS.md §F-11's 'v1.3 (pilot), n=5' row (29% acceptance, 10 escaped, median wall 37.5s / median cost $0.064, reconciling to the five scored:true pre-fix rows in results/runs.jsonl); both of FC-01's registered tools (init-run.mjs, hooks/gate-zerowork.mjs) are verifiably absent at a280e86 (git cat-file -e), which is what makes this a legitimate before-state

current.method: Corrected count, replacing the retired narrated-predicate rate (see superseded[], cause instrument-change): sdd-harness-bench @ 16fb752, arm-tagged rows in results/runs.jsonl (arm=day2-armA, n=3), harness_build v1.6.3+e08082c685dc (v1.6.3 (e08082c685dc) packed), cost $5.32. Rep 1 ('built_and_failed') wrote one file (intake.md) and shipped zero product code — 0 product writes — scoring the baseline's own acceptance 0.2857 with 10 escaped defects; the retired predicate (writes===0) missed this because the intake write itself makes writes!==0, so it was recorded 'not narrated'. Counted honestly by what the run actually shipped, rep 1 is a shipped-nothing case; reps 2 and 3 ('ok', 'ok') shipped real product code and are not. The arm is 1/3 shipped-nothing, Fisher exact one-tailed vs the 5/5 baseline p=0.1071 (not the retired rate's p=0.018) — this does not meet the sampled-reduction exit criterion. Caveat unchanged: one feature, one model, an author-run benchmark — FINDINGS.md §F-11's limit travels with this number. MODEL SCOPE, established 2026-08-07 (rev 5 Stage 3), which is why model_scope on both rates reads claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 rather than being left to a reader's assumption: this class does not occur on Sonnet. The corrected predicate was implemented in the benchmark as product_writes (writes excluding every arm's declared state roots and its planning prose) with a shipped_nothing mode meaning product_writes===0 (sdd-harness-bench @ d3787fa, runner/lib/transcript-metrics.mjs, 76 self-test checks), then applied to every surviving transcript joined to results/runs.jsonl by each row's own recorded transcript path — 228 of 230 rows joined, 102 of them scored. Result: of 50 scored claude-sonnet-5 rows across all arms, shipped_nothing occurs 0 times; of the 8 scored shapeup-sdlc Sonnet rows every single one made at least one product write (3, 8, 2, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2); at the pre-fix build a280e86 itself Sonnet has n=2 (f1-todo-cli 3 product writes, f2-budgets 8), both scoring 1.0 acceptance. The same predicate on Haiku shapeup-sdlc rows finds 7 of 16 shipping nothing (5 narrated at 0 writes, 2 shipped_nothing at 1 write). The n=3 Sonnet arm the plan costed at $5.8 was NOT bought and is not purchasable with today's adapter: the adapter requires .shapeup/*/receipt.json as run evidence, that receipt is written by init-run.mjs which first exists at 36521ba (v1.4.0), and the string receipt.json appears nowhere in the tree at a280e86 — so every rep at the pre-fix build is scored harness_unreachable and excluded by PROTOCOL §8, as 14 rows already in the record were. a280e86 is the pre-fix build precisely because it predates init-run.mjs, so the adapter demands the artifact whose absence defines the build; the two are mutually exclusive by construction. This is the plan's own §7 falsifier and its disposition-table row 4 — instrument fault, discard the arm, change nothing — reached for $0 rather than $5.8.

error_predicate.counts: Runs that were allowed to finish and produced no deliverable. `product_writes` counts writes to files that could plausibly ship, excluding every arm's declared state roots (.shapeup/, .shapeup-sdlc/, shapeup/) and its planning prose — so the intake write that made the retired `writes === 0` predicate miss rep 1 no longer conceals a run that shipped nothing. It is null rather than 0 when a transcript's write targets cannot be classified, so zero is claimed only where zero was observed. The STOPPED_FROM_OUTSIDE guard excludes every status meaning the run was killed rather than finished — without it the handoff protocol's 87 deliberate mid-run cuts, which have by design written nothing yet, were the largest and entirely spurious population in the record.

classes.predicate_independence: The predicate is computed in a different repository from the tool it measures, by a scorer the tool never runs and cannot see: `failureMode()` reads the transcript after the fact, from `sdd-harness-bench`, over rows joined by each run's own recorded transcript path. The harness under test emits no field this predicate reads — it cannot mark itself as having shipped. Known and unfixed limit, recorded because it is the attack surface: hand-written harness scripts at product-shaped paths (`run-init.mjs`, `spike-*.mjs` at the workspace root) are `.mjs` outside the excluded roots and still count, so `product_writes` is an UPPER bound on real deliverables. A harness that wrote such files would exit this class exactly as `writes === 0` was exited — which is why this field exists rather than a claim that the predicate is unsteerable.

superseded.method: sdd-harness-bench @ dff1bf2, results/v15-haiku-f2.log (FINDINGS.md §F-11's post-fix reps, 14/14 acceptance x3); failureMode() classifies all three runs 'ok', none 'narrated' — 0/3; Fisher exact one-tailed vs the 5/5 baseline p=0.0179, one-sided 95% upper bound on the post-fix rate 0.632, so 'the rate fell from 1.0' is supported and 'this now happens under 5% of the time' is not. the contradiction: these rows are labelled harness_build a280e86 in runs.jsonl and each recorded receipt ✓, but the receipt is written by init-run.mjs, which does not exist at a280e86 (git cat-file -e) — a run cannot emit an artifact from a script its build lacks, so the a280e86 label is refuted and harness_build is recorded null here rather than repeating a build id this run cannot have come from

RETIRED (instrument-change): this rate counted failureMode()==='narrated', whose predicate is writes===0 — and this harness's own intake write (the receipt init-run.mjs writes at run start, and the intake.md document itself) makes writes!==0 for every run that reaches the pipeline at all, foreclosing the predicate from ever firing true on this harness's own output; see Stage 1's predicate_independence field for the general question this instance answers. Original measurement: sdd-harness-bench @ 16fb752, arm-tagged rows in results/runs.jsonl (arm=day2-armA, n=3): failureMode() classifies all three runs 'built_and_failed', 'ok', 'ok' — 0/3 narrated, 3/3 receipts present, harness_build v1.6.3+e08082c685dc (v1.6.3 (e08082c685dc) packed), cost $5.32. Pre-registered attribution (contract.md Stage 2, decided joint): Arm B — grant withheld — recorded 0/3 receipts and 0 scored rows; init-run.mjs never ran there, so FC-01's registered tools never fired on that arm. The acceptance those Arm B runs would have scored is 0.286 x3, the pilot baseline's own 29% reproduced at zero variance — Arm B's finding is unaffected by this withdrawal and stays attributed via co_attributed_to. Caveat: one feature, one model, an author-run benchmark — FINDINGS.md §F-11's limit travels with this number.

classes.error_class: Silently inert enforcement — a guard that is installed, documented and green in CI, but never actually fires under an ordinary install
classes.description: Audit F-16: 26 enforcement points sat inert behind 610 green structural checks in v1.4.0. The checks proved the files existed and parsed; nothing proved the guard was reached at runtime in the shape a user installs.

discovered_by.quote: indistinguishability is how 26 enforcement points sat inert behind 610 green checks in 1.4.0

tool.name: permission grant + packed-distributable + hook decision receipts
tool.permissions: `npx shapeup-sdlc init` writes permissions.allow into .claude/settings.json so plugin-shipped entry points can run at all; without it a headless run cannot take its first step (measured: 26 approval denials in one session).

result_confirmation.ref: structural §11d (the PACKED distributable — the shape a user actually installs), §43 (every documented invocation matches the permission grant), §44 (every hook records a decision: allow, deny and error stop looking identical)

baseline.method: count of enforcement points found inert under an ordinary install at v1.4.0; a COUNT, not a rate in [0,1]; counted by the F-16 audit, dated to the commit that resolved it (27deb1b, 'fix: v1.4.1 — the enforcement layer was inert under an ordinary install'), 2026-07-28

current.method: structural §11a scans 33 .mjs modules under bin/ hooks/ skills/ scripts/ for the broken same-line import.meta.url / process.argv[1] main guard and finds 1 hand-rolled occurrence, inside the shared helper's (skills/tech-lead/scripts/lib/is-main.mjs) own explanation of the bug — zero offenders outside it. §11b separately executes the 22 entry points in ENTRY_POINTS (tests/structural/11-is-main.mjs) through a symlinked directory and a directory whose name contains a space, and every one behaves like its real-path invocation. Two denominators, kept distinct: 33 modules scanned for the pattern, 22 entry points execution-probed — not the population the F-16 audit's 26 inert guards were drawn from, and not compared to it.

error_predicate.expression: offender ⇔ a .mjs file under bin/ hooks/ skills/ scripts/ (outside skills/tech-lead/scripts/lib/is-main.mjs) carries import.meta.url and process.argv[1] on the same line — the fragile, symlink-unsafe main guard §11a scans for
error_predicate.counts: offenders.length — the number of scanned .mjs modules that hand-roll the broken main guard; FC-02's current.value (0) is this count found outside the shared helper

classes.error_class: Lenient judge — a build with a live acceptance violation is passed because its own suite is green and its boxes are ticked
classes.description: The failure mode the anti-leniency fixture is built around: multiples of 15 print Fizz, the in-repo suite probes only n<=10 and stays green, every AC box ships ticked, and the source reads like textbook FizzBuzz. A judge that reads instead of probing ships the defect.

discovered_by.quote: A lenient LLM judge ('the tests pass, the boxes are ticked, the code looks right → PASS') ships the bug.

tool.name: process oracle + T0 citation requirement
tool.permissions: Runs the built artifact as a subprocess against a declared contract; the judge must additionally cite a T0 artifact whose sha256 it recomputes from disk rather than trusting a handed hash.

result_confirmation.ref: structural §13 — the planted-bug fixture PASSes the correct control and FAILs the buggy build on TS-04, so the fixture cannot rot into a non-discriminating state

classes.error_class: Fabricated evidence — a baseline that carries numbers no run produced
classes.description: Audit F1: the prior roadmap claimed a measured evidence layer that was never committed, and its headline TPR≈0 was a proxy artifact — it counted slash-command self-invocation rather than real Skill-tool activation, so it measured nothing.

discovered_by.quote: The earlier measurement counted slash-command self-invocation, not Skill-tool activation, so it measured nothing real.

tool.name: baseline honesty invariant
tool.permissions: Read-only over evals/baselines/*.json; fails CI when an `unmeasured` baseline carries results or a `measured` one lacks method + measured_at.

result_confirmation.ref: structural §16 (trigger-eval baseline), §48 (Day-1 loop baseline + Day-2 register held to the same invariant)

baseline.method: count of fabricated baselines shipped before the invariant existed (the F1 incident); a COUNT, not a rate; counted by the F1 audit that first found the claimed evidence layer unbacked by any committed artifact (2026-06-26), the finding now documented at evals/README.md

current.method: fabricated baselines present across the three baseline files now under the invariant (trigger-evals, skill-loop, failure-classes); mechanically enforced, so the value is structural rather than sampled

error_predicate.expression: fabricated ⇔ (status==="unmeasured" && results!==null) || (status==="measured" && !(results && method && measured_at)) — a baseline record claiming a state its own fields contradict
error_predicate.counts: the number of baseline records, across the trigger-eval, skill-loop and failure-classes baselines now held to the same invariant, that violate it; FC-04's current.value (0 of 3) is this count

classes.error_class: Sibling-stealing skill description — a description that activates on its own examples but also on a sibling skill's queries
classes.description: With thirteen skills whose domains adjoin, a description tuned only against its own positives can capture a neighbour's work. The cross-skill hard negatives exist to make that visible.

discovered_by.quote: a description that triggers on its own examples but *also* steals its siblings' is not actually discriminating

tool.name: trigger-eval harness
tool.permissions: Spawns headless `claude --plugin-dir . -p <query> --max-turns 8`; requires Claude auth; aborts and writes nothing when a run produces no parseable model events.

result_confirmation.ref: structural §16 — datasets well-formed, >=4 positives + >=3 cross-skill negatives per skill, every expected_other a real skill

baseline.method: the prior TPR≈0 was a proxy artifact and is NOT usable as a baseline — it is withdrawn, not carried forward

current.method: false-positive rate across 75 cross-skill hard negatives, claude headless --max-turns 8 --concurrency 4, real Skill-tool activation

classes.error_class: Malformed work order reaching a worker — a worker acts on an order nobody compiled or validated
classes.description: Before the envelope port, a worker could be dispatched with a hand-written or partial order. The failure is silent: the worker does something plausible against an under-specified contract.

discovered_by.quote: Prevents: a worker acting on an order nobody compiled

tool.name: validate-envelope PreToolUse hook
tool.permissions: PreToolUse hard-deny on any worker dispatch whose WorkOrder is missing or fails its schema; guards both directions of the port (WorkResult on the way back).

result_confirmation.ref: structural §20 (envelope schemas discriminate), §21 (compile-order assembles a schema-valid, fact-only order), §24 (validation discriminates through the $ref chain)

classes.error_class: Cross-scope write corruption — a worker writes outside its scope's substrate and overwrites another scope's work
classes.description: With per-scope parallel or sequential work over one repository, an unconstrained worker can edit files another scope owns; the loser's completions vanish without any error.

discovered_by.quote: Prevents: … a scope overwriting another's work

tool.name: sandbox-guard
tool.permissions: PreToolUse deny on every write outside the active scope's allowed_file_substrate; the whitelist is declared in the committed scope contract.

result_confirmation.ref: structural §17 — denies an out-of-substrate write and allows an in-substrate one

classes.error_class: Unstable judge — the same criterion is graded PASS in one run and FAIL in the next, with no change to the build
classes.description: A single-judge architecture is only as good as the judge's stability. An undetected flip means the verdict is noise, and a run that happened to catch the good draw ships.

tool.name: verdict ledger
tool.permissions: Append-only JSONL in the gitignored run tier; forces a flipped criterion's confidence to `low` and exits non-zero on a flipping ledger.

result_confirmation.ref: structural §15 — flags a PASS→FAIL flip across runs, leaves stable criteria untouched, exits non-zero on a flipping ledger and zero on a stable one
